# DevOps and SRE Interview

> The loop round by round: troubleshooting, Linux and networking, SRE system design, and incident response. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Cheat sheets

- [Availability Numbers](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/availability-numbers.md): Availability is the share of time, or the share of requests, in which a service works.
- [Common Mistakes in DevOps and SRE Interviews](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/common-mistakes.md): Most rejected candidates in these loops knew the tools.
- [DevOps vs SRE](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/devops-vs-sre.md): DevOps is a way of working in which the people who build software and the people who run it share responsibility for delivery.
- [Four-Week Preparation Plan](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/four-week-plan.md): This plan prepares a working engineer for a DevOps or SRE loop in four weeks at about eight hours a week.
- [Linux Commands for Troubleshooting](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/linux-commands-for-troubleshooting.md): In a troubleshooting round, a command is useful only when the candidate can state the question it answers.
- [DevOps and SRE Interview Question Bank](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/question-bank.md): This page lists 60 questions that candidates commonly report, grouped by round.

## Concepts

- [Capacity Planning](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/capacity-planning.md): Capacity planning is the work of deciding how much hardware a service needs to meet its targets at peak load, with enough spare to survive a failure.
- [CI/CD and Deployment Strategies](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/ci-cd-and-deployment-strategies.md): Continuous integration (CI) builds and tests every change as soon as it is merged.
- [Containers and Kubernetes](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/containers-and-kubernetes.md): A container is a process that runs with its own view of the file system, the network, and the process list.
- [Infrastructure as Code](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/infrastructure-as-code.md): Infrastructure as code means describing servers, networks, and other resources in files that are kept in version control and applied by a tool.
- [Observability](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/observability.md): Observability is the ability to understand what a system is doing from the data it emits.
- [Postmortems](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/postmortems.md): A postmortem is a written review of an incident: what happened, why, what it cost, and what will change.
- [SLIs, SLOs, and Error Budgets](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/slis-slos-and-error-budgets.md): A service level indicator (SLI) is a measurement of how well a service behaves.
- [Toil and Automation](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/concepts/toil-and-automation.md): Toil is operational work that is manual, repetitive, and automatable, and that grows as the service grows.

## Rounds

- [The Behavioral Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/behavioral.md): The behavioral round asks how a candidate acted in real situations.
- [The Coding and Scripting Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/coding-and-scripting.md): The coding round in a DevOps or SRE loop usually asks for a practical program, such as a log parser or a small command-line tool.
- [The Incident Response Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/incident-response.md): The incident response round tests whether a candidate can lead while production is failing.
- [The DevOps and SRE Interview Loop](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/interview-loop.md): An interview loop is the full sequence of interviews for one role, and each interview in it is a round.
- [The Linux and Networking Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/linux-and-networking.md): The Linux and networking round checks whether a candidate understands how the operating system and the network behave.
- [The SRE System Design Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/sre-system-design.md): The SRE system design round asks for a design and then asks how that design fails, how it is released, and how it is measured.
- [The Troubleshooting Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview/blob/main/rounds/troubleshooting.md): In the troubleshooting round, the interviewer describes a failure and the candidate investigates it one step at a time.
